decision: The script that changes a task's record also makes the paired backlog change, in the same process and before it reports success.
alternatives: A later agent turn moves the backlog item.
A printed reminder asks the agent to move the item.
tradeoff: Spawn and teardown refuse rather than report success when the backlog transition cannot land, so a backlog fault can stop a dispatch or a cleanup.
reversal_cost: High in effect: spawn, teardown and bootstrap all rely on the pairing (inferred from the cited header, not stated by the authors).

decision: A spawn at declared capacity exits 75 before it creates any brief, endpoint, worktree, record or backlog move.
alternatives: Mark the item blocked (the cited text says it stays queued rather than blocked).
tradeoff: The item is left exactly as queued, but nothing in the cited text retries it; the agent must dispatch it again.
reversal_cost: Moderate (inferred): callers of the spawn script and its batch mode rely on exit 75.

decision: Isolated work is dispatched at once with no concurrency cap; overlap is a risk signal, not a reason to wait.
alternatives: Wait for overlapping work to finish (the cited text rejects same-file editing alone as a reason to serialize).
tradeoff: More parallel work and more rebases or conflicts for the delivery path to reconcile; the cited text accepts this when each change can be validated alone.
reversal_cost: Low (inferred): the rule is prose, and a declared project capacity already caps it in code.

decision: A spawn that cannot take the shared project lock exits at once instead of waiting.
alternatives: Wait for the lock until it is free.
tradeoff: The caller sees an error and must try again, but a stuck holder cannot hang the spawn (inferred).
reversal_cost: Low (inferred): one acquire call and its error branch.

decision: When a backlog item is still an open captain call, teardown reopens it with the deliverable recorded instead of closing it.
alternatives: Close the item as cleanup finishes, as for any other task.
tradeoff: The captain's question survives cleanup, but the item stays open after the worktree is gone, and --force cannot close it; only the captain's answer does.
reversal_cost: Moderate (inferred): the pending-close record carries a retain mode that the session-start replay and the captain-hold script both rely on.
authors_say: the policy holds the very work item a question gates and cleanup must never retire the captain's own question

decision: A PR-based ship frees its place when its ready PR is recorded, not when the PR merges.
alternatives: Hold the place until the work is merged and cleaned up, as a local-only ship and a scout do.
tradeoff: More work can start while earlier PRs wait on review, but a local-only ship or a scout, which record no PR, keep their place until cleanup.
reversal_cost: Low (inferred): one test of the recorded PR in the occupancy count.
authors_say: after which the worker waits on review or merge and no longer uses local resources
